title: ALMA Observations of Polarized 872 μm Dust Emission from the Protostellar Systems VLA 1623 and L1527
question: What mechanism produces the 872 um polarized dust emission in young protostellar disks (VLA 1623, L1527): magnetically aligned grains, self-scattering, or radiative-flux alignment?

what.value: ALMA 1.3 mm continuum of VLA 1623 used for proper motion

evidence.quote: By combining the data from ALMA 1.3 mm continuum observations from (cite: mu13) with ours

what.value: L1527 disk temperature profile from CO isotopologues

evidence.quote: the radial temperature profile of the disk of L1527 has been estimated from observations of optically thick $^{13}$CO($J=2-1$) and C$^{18}$O($J=2-1$) emission

recipe.method: clean in four Stokes with multiscale after phase-only self-cal; natural and Briggs weightings

recipe.goal: Make PI, PA and fraction maps
recipe.method: immath: PI=sqrt(Q^2+U^2), debiased; masked below 5 sigma in PI and 3 sigma in I
image-plane elliptical Gaussian fits deconvolved from beam, in I and PI; CB disk by subtracting Aa/Ab model from visibilities, tapering and fitting

recipe.goal: Test polarization angle vs disk minor axis
recipe.method: PI-weighted mean angle within 0.1 arcsec of PI peak; KS and Anderson-Darling tests vs uniform offsets

recipe.goal: Estimate optical depth and disk stability
recipe.method: Brightness temperature from peak surface brightness compared with kinetic temperature; Toomre Q for the circumbinary disk from optically thin mass
assumptions: kappa = 10 (nu/1 THz)^beta cm2/g, beta=1, gas-to-dust 100, Td = 30 K, central mass 0.15 Msun
